catholic-encyclopedia-1913-john-floyd:
John Floyd was an English Jesuit missionary and controversialist who wrote under a string of pen names. Born in Cambridgeshire in 1572, he studied at the Jesuit college at Eu, at Reims, and at Rome, where he joined the Society of Jesus in 1592. As a missionary in England from 1606 he was arrested at Worcester, imprisoned for a year, and banished for life with forty-six other priests.

Teaching at St. Omer, then back on the English mission, he was often captured and bought his way free from pursuivants. His Overthrow of the Protestant Pulpit Babels of 1612 answered Crawshaw and drew a reply from Sir Edward Hoby, sparking a pamphlet war. He then wrote four works against the apostate Archbishop de Dominis, and died at St. Omer in 1649, his works sometimes misattributed to Robert Jennison.
